clue.text: Sentence beginning with this kind of punishment?

definitions.text: Sentence beginning with this kind of punishment?

parts.words: Sentence beginning with this kind of punishment?
parts.note: a sentence of writing begins with an upper-case letter, and the gravest punishment a court can pass is the death penalty; one word fits both

explanation.surface: A judge musing on what sort of punishment a sentence starts with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' reads as a court's judgment, but the first sense is a written sentence, whose first letter is of this kind; the second is the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters open written sentences, and capital punishment means execution.

clue.text: Eccentric patient in a car

definitions.note: a phrase for a component found in a car engine

parts.note: a crank is an eccentric person
a doctor's case is a patient

explanation.surface: An odd patient sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' and 'patient' look like adjective and noun, but each gives a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The crankcase is the housing for the crankshaft in a car engine.

clue.text: Arrest upset US lawyer married in Germany

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place found in Germany

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word runs upward

parts.note: to arrest is to stop
a DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: An American lawyer arrested after marrying in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns STOP into POTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a German city near Berlin, site of the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Bloomer causes great pain to one learner

parts.note: to torment is to cause great pain
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A blunder that hurts one student badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Pike (anagram clue)

indicators.note: the clue itself says the next word is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish named, with a note that this is a letter-shuffling clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is candid: 'anagram' rearranges the word 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Luce is an old name for the pike, a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Fair takes in a French funambulist

parts.note: fair hair is blond
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairground that brings in a French tightrope act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a fete taking in an act, but it is the hair colour; 'takes' just joins it to IN. Charles Blondin was the French acrobat who crossed Niagara Falls on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Blondin was a celebrated nineteenth-century French tightrope walker.

clue.text: Without locks? Without any restraint at all

explanation.surface: Two senses of being without something.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is hairless on top; to go at something bald-headed means recklessly, with no restraint.

clue.text: Prepared to get shot. in attack?

explanation.surface: Someone ready to be shot in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor on set is ready for filming; an onset is an assault or beginning.

clue.text: Decline to allow a little water

parts.note: to drop is to decline or fall
let means allow

explanation.surface: Refusing to permit even a little water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refuse, but it is a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a tiny drop of liquid.

clue.text: Can get upset about-chemical

indicators.note: get upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word runs upward

parts.note: a tin is a can
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone who gets upset about a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical used in gunpowder.

clue.text: In a monastery garden?

indicators.note: the letters sought sit inside the word monastery, as the clue's preposition says

explanation.surface: Asking what might grow in a cloister's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits inside 'monastery', and the whole clue also describes a flower one could find growing in such a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden flower, the kind that might grow in a cloister bed.

clue.text: Plant on which a horse is first raised

definitions.text: Plant on which a horse is first raised

parts.words: Plant on which a horse is first raised
parts.note: a young male horse lifts its hoof; the name of that limb belonging to a young horse is also a yellow-flowered weed

explanation.surface: A horse lifting one hoof before stepping off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a young horse's foot, the one 'first raised' as it moves; the name is also a wild plant with yellow flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coltsfoot is a yellow-flowered weed once used in cough remedies.

clue.text: Organ of a sort

explanation.surface: Describing an organ of a certain type.
explanation.definitionFit: The bean-shaped organ filters blood; 'of that kidney' is an old idiom for of that kind or temperament.

clue.text: Tactful evasion when golf-ball landed in the snow

parts.note: everything in snow looks white
a golf ball's lie is where it has come to rest

explanation.surface: A golfer fibbing tactfully about where the ball fell in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the 'lie' is the spot where the ball comes to rest, and in snow that spot is white.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmless untruth told to spare feelings is a polite way of dodging the truth.

clue.text: Lavish display reduced to show end of space trip

parts.note: to make a splash is to put on a big show
down means reduced, as in prices down

explanation.surface: A big show cut short to mark the end of a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' reads as cut down to size, but it gives DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a spacecraft landing in the sea at the end of its flight.

clue.text: Let in a doctor, retired, it appears

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the doctor's letters run backwards

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A receptionist letting in a doctor who has just retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns MD into DM.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them entry.

clue.text: A 'grim pact arranged with this sanction

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase 'pragmatic sanction', an imperial decree on a state matter

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim treaty is drawn up with the approval of some authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges AGRIMPACT. A pragmatic sanction was a sovereign's decree, most famously Charles VI's of 1713 on the Habsburg succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Historians use the phrase 'pragmatic sanction' for a ruler's decree settling a state question.

clue.text: Airy accommodation for, players?

parts.note: airy suggests fresh space, but here airs are tunes, and the players are musicians, so a room where tunes are played

explanation.surface: Asking for a well-ventilated room for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airy' suggests ventilation, but it means full of airs, that is, tunes, for the players.
explanation.definitionFit: A music room is a room set aside for playing or practising instruments.

clue.text: Cool, one has gathered

explanation.surface: Calmly, someone has gathered something together.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected person is calm and composed; collected also means gathered up.

clue.text: Absolve former copper head, about fifty

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: Clearing a former police officer, a head of about fifty years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's symbol; 'about' is only a link here, as L comes right before PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear someone of blame.

clue.text: I entered dream-home here in Spain

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a region of Spain

indicators.note: entered means went into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a castle in Spain is an idiom for a daydream, a dream home

explanation.surface: Someone who walks into the home of their dreams in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castles in Spain' is an idiom for daydreams, like castles in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile is a historic kingdom of central Spain.

clue.text: Prophetic book-seller

parts.note: the legendary Cumaean prophetess offered nine books of prophecy to King Tarquin of Rome and sold him the last three

explanation.surface: A bookshop owner who can see the future.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend tells how the Cumaean prophetess sold the Sibylline Books to Tarquin, burning six when he haggled.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world.

clue.text: Beds for some schoolboys, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, giving the same sound

parts.note: boarders are pupils who live at school

explanation.surface: Beds for some of the schoolboys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' look like dormitory beds, but they are flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden borders are narrow beds along the edge of a lawn.

clue.text: A drink Ben has' it as cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Ben orders a drink and has it mixed as a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as cocktail' rearranges BENHASIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green wormwood-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: Scope of a biter's complaint

explanation.surface: Wondering what a biter might complain about.
explanation.definitionFit: One's ambit is one's range or reach; read as two words it is the moan of the bitten.

clue.text: Features connected with certain spectacles

explanation.surface: Faces linked to particular eyeglasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial features include these; pince-nez, French for pinch-nose, clip onto them.

clue.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

definitions.text: What many, in panic, make themselves

parts.words: What many, in panic, make themselves
parts.note: to flee danger is idiomatically to make oneself hard to find, a phrase built on an adjective meaning in short supply

explanation.surface: How people react when panic sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make yourself scarce' means go away quickly, what frightened crowds do.
explanation.definitionFit: Making oneself scarce is an idiom for getting away fast.

clue.text: Simple lines, eh? Give: it up!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the whole run turns over

parts.note: BR is British Rail, railway lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: Simple lines, eh? Give it up!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give it up!' turns BREH over in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old name for a medicinal plant.

clue.text: Riverside rock butterfly

parts.note: the brim is the edge or bank, as of a river
stone means rock

explanation.surface: A butterfly settled on a rock by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIM for an edge or bank is an old sense, as in a river brimming over its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a sulphur-yellow European butterfly.

clue.text: Some cricket Test opener, that's evident

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

indicators.note: opener names the first letter of the word Test

explanation.surface: A cricket Test's opening batsman whose quality is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like an opening batsman in a Test match, but it takes the first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is out in the open and plain to see.

clue.text: The fifth betrayal still remembered

parts.note: the rhyme 'Remember, remember the fifth of November' recalls the Gunpowder Plot of 1605 and calls it gunpowder ... and plot

explanation.surface: A betrayal on the fifth that is still commemorated.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night, 5 November, marks the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament; the rhyme names 'gunpowder treason and plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler.

clue.text: One of nine in plot appears stupefied

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: One of nine conspirators in a plot looks dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy but is a flower bed; the nine are the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered or dazed.
